findings.title: A box holding tokens (a token pool's way back, often marked mixed) is left out of the box order, so orders a and b and the parts merge a box of unknown making, or more ADA boxes than pay, ahead of it
findings.scenario:
Case A, unknown making ahead of mixed. The private balance holds:
- O: 5 ₳ made private (public:0)
- K: a plain box's way back of 9.71 ₳ (box:k, lovejoin)
- W: a box of unknown making of 9.71 ₳ (box:w+unknown:w: one Bring every box back now took that the records don't place, or a planted one)
- T: a token pool box's way back, marked mixed (mixedBox), 4.15 ₳ plus its token. `adds` is about 2.5 ₳.
The user sends 16 ₳ to a Seedelf.
1. Step 1: every single UTxO is at or under the 16 ₳ floor, so each is Skipped. Step 2: every class has one row, so nothing builds.
2. Order a is now [O, K, W, T]. T is not in box_list, so place = usize::MAX. O+K is 14.71 ₳ (Skipped), and O+K+W builds.
3. more_mixed(2) over K (rank 1) and W (rank 2) gives no choice.
4. The Send spends W.
5. At 1e1b0647, order a was [O, T, K, W], because Pay ranks Mixed 4 before Lovejoin 5. It built O+T+K. That is the same box count, one of the two boxes mixed, and no box of unknown making. The change of 2.5 ₳ carries T's token.

Case B, more boxes than pay. O 5 ₳, two plain 4.71 ₳ boxes, and T, the way back of a 9 ₳ token pool box: 8.65 ₳ plus its token, adds about 7.1 ₳. A Send of 11 ₳ now spends O+K1+K2 (two boxes). Before it spent O+T (one mixed box).

The same holds for a funding (Fund: Mixed 2 < Lovejoin 3) and for payments in parts. Worth::apart lists only token-free tier-2 classes in `boxes`, and every other tier-2 class sorts at usize::MAX, after every ADA box, a box of unknown making included.
findings.who: Nobody has to act. It hits an ordinary Send, Make public or funding that needs a second box, for a user who holds a token pool's way back next to a box of unknown making. Mallory can supply the box of unknown making by depositing under the user's register; the user's own box the records don't place (after a restore, or taken by Bring every box back now) works too.
findings.evidence:
- build.rs:3042-3043 `let is_box = |u: &UtxoResponse| tier(u) == 2 && !holds_tokens(u); let box_list ... .filter(|u| is_box(u))`. Only these get a `place` and `weights` (:3045-3054).
- :3065-3070 `place` is `.unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` for anything else.
- :3072-3081 by_history key `(last(u), tier(u), place(u), !joins_base(u), purpose.rank(&class(u)), holds_tokens(u), ...)`. `place` comes before the rank, so in tier 2 every ADA box, box_rank 2 included, sorts ahead of a tier-2 UTxO holding tokens, mixed or not. by_tier (:3084-3092) does the same.
- 1e1b0647 by_history (:2935-2944) was `(last(u), tier(u), !joins_base(u), purpose.rank(&class(u)), holds_tokens(u), ...)`, which put a Mixed one (Pay 4, Fund 2, Mint 0) before every Lovejoin box.
- wasm lib.rs:4145-4147 `.filter(|&i| tier(&classes[i].1) == 2 && ada_alone(&classes[i].1))`. :4169 `places.get(&c.id).copied().unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` comes before `histories.rank_of(rows[0])`.
- lovejoin.ts:8238-8244 classes every way back alike, a token pool's included (`mixedBoxOf(s, box) ? mixedBox(built.txHash) : ...`), and the way back keeps its token (`built.token`, :8262).
- box_value.rs:62: a token pool's box holds up to 9 ₳ (4.5 ₳ suggested).
- `adds` (build.rs:420-426) is its ADA less its token's least, positive, so the box is not `last`.
- The docs claim otherwise:
  - architecture.md:144: "a box someone else put in, its way back tagged Unknown, is never merged ahead of another box"
  - privacy.md:173: "among as many, one the wallet knows is mixed first, and one tagged Unknown too after every other box"
  - privacy-policy.md:93: "A session's funding and a private payment, too, take a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of"
- No test merges a tier-2 UTxO holding tokens. apart_test.rs, mint_test.rs mod apart and box_order_tests use ADA-only boxes.
findings.fix:
Bring tier-2 UTxOs holding tokens into the box order:
- Weigh each by `adds` (its ADA less its tokens' least). Rank each by box_rank, 0 when Mixed or when it joins the base.
- Then `place` and more_mixed cover them in orders a and b.
- Worth::apart drops the `ada_alone` filter and weighs a class by its total `adds`.
- c's j prefix can stay ADA-only.

Narrower option: key tier 2 in a and b on `(box_rank == 2, place-or-rank)`, so a known token box sits before every box of unknown making, and say in the docs that a box holding tokens comes after the boxes of ADA alone.

Test (mint_test mod apart): O 5 ₳, K 9.71 ₳ plain, W 9.71 ₳ unplaced, T 4.15 ₳ + 1 token, mixed. A 16 ₳ Send and an 11 ₳ funding spend T and K, never W.
findings.owner_question: Is a token pool's way back a box to the merge order (a mixed one first among as many, ahead of any box of unknown making)? Or should boxes holding tokens stay after every box of ADA alone, with the docs saying so?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD (550a368f). I traced it end to end, ran it, and found no guard that stops it.

1. A token pool's way back is a tier-2 UTxO that holds a token.
   - wasm/src/lovejoin.rs `withdraw_in` returns `WithdrawResult.token`: "A token pool's token, into the same register".
   - lovejoin.ts:8238 classes the way back `mixedBoxOf(s, box) ? mixedBox(built.txHash) : ...`, which is `{id: "box:<tx>", origin: "mixed"}`. `mixedBoxOf` (:2467) works for any pool. :8260 keeps `built.token`.
   - `Purpose::tier` puts Lovejoin and Mixed in tier 2.
2. A Send reaches core's `apart` with that UTxO among the others. transfer.ts `build` → `buildTransferParts` → `build_transfer` → `transfer_spend`, which calls `build::transfer_apart(..., histories(Purpose::Pay, ...))` (lib.rs:3396) → `select_script_inputs`, with floor = `paid_out` → `apart`.
   - `readContract` does not filter out UTxOs holding tokens.
   - `blind()` is false.
   - `adds(T)` = 2,503,580 lovelace, which is positive, so T is not `last`.
3. In `apart`, a box holding tokens is never a box:
   - build.rs:3042 `let is_box = |u| tier(u) == 2 && !holds_tokens(u);` and :3043 `box_list` filter by it, so only these get a `place` and a weight (:3045-3054).
   - :3065-3070 `place` is `.unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` for anything else.
   - :3071-3081 by_history's key is `(last, tier, place, !joins_base, purpose.rank, ...)`; by_tier (:3083-3092) is the same. `place` comes before the rank, so in tier 2 every ADA-only box, one of unknown making included, sorts ahead of T.
   - `more_mixed_built` (:2889) picks only from `box_list` and `weights`, so it never offers T.
4. Case A as traced, which the run below confirms:
   - Each UTxO alone is 16 ₳ or less, so step 1 skips them all; each class has one row, so step 2 builds nothing.
   - Order a is [O, K, W, T]. O+K is 14.71 ₳ (Skipped); O+K+W builds.
   - `more_mixed(weights, 2)` finds no mixed box among K and W, so no other choice.
   - Result: O+K+W, where O+K+T builds with the same box count.
5. Case B: order a is [O, K1, K2, T] and builds O+K1+K2. O+T alone builds (checked with `transfer_from(...).estimate()`).
6. Round five caused it. The same test passes against 1e1b0647's build.rs (A spends O,K,T; B spends O,T), because there the rank (Mixed 4 before Lovejoin 5) ordered tier 2. dc31711b's `place` changed that.
7. The parts path does the same. In wasm `Worth::apart`, lib.rs:4140-4147 filter `tier == 2 && ada_alone`, and :4169 puts `places.get(&c.id)...unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` ahead of `rank_of`. A payment's parts order comes out [O, K, W, T] for both Pay and Fund.
8. The docs say otherwise:
   - architecture.md:144: "a box someone else put in, its way back tagged Unknown, is never merged ahead of another box"
   - privacy.md:173: "among as many, one the wallet knows is mixed first, and one tagged Unknown too after every other box"
   - privacy-policy.md:93: "A session's funding and a private payment, too, take a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of"
   - No doc says that boxes holding tokens come after the ADA-only boxes.
9. The fixer knew. round5.json's "left" says "tier-2 UTxOs holding tokens now come after the pure-ADA boxes (before, they were interleaved by rank)", and lib.rs:4137-4139 says "those holding tokens after them". The docs were never told.

Who can cause it: anyone holding a token pool's way back. Token pools are capped at 9 ₳ a box, 4.5 ₳ suggested. Retired tokenV1 pools' boxes still come back, and v2 token pools can be launched.
- Case A needs a box of unknown making beside it: Mallory's deposit under a copied register, or the user's own box the records don't place (Bring every box back now, a restore).
- Case B needs no stranger.

Why medium: by default the spend merges a box of unknown making ahead of a mixed box, or merges an extra box, and the three docs above claim more than the code does. No funds are lost, and the review's note still names what is merged.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Option 1 is a full fix. I prototyped it in the scratch copy only. With it, both new tests pass, and so do mint_test (66), apart_test (17), merge_test (6), selection_integration (8), orders_test (32), most_test (5), stranger_token_pile_test (1) and seedelf-wasm --lib (22).

Core (build.rs):
1. Pass `params` into `apart`: change select_script_inputs:2792 to `apart(params, mandatory, rest, ...)` and add `params: &ProtocolParameters` as `apart`'s first argument.
2. :3042 becomes `let is_box = |u: &UtxoResponse| tier(u) == 2 && !last(u);`. A tier-2 UTxO that adds less than nothing stays last and is no box.
3. In `weights` (:3045-3054), weigh each box by what it adds, not by its lovelace: `adds(params, u).map_or(lovelace_in(u), |a| u128::try_from(a.max(0)).unwrap_or(0))`, with the rank as now (0 when `ties_nothing`, else `box_rank`).
4. That is the whole code change for core. `place`, a and b, c's j prefix and `more_mixed_built` then cover token boxes, and c's rests (`largest`, `tokens_last`) drop them because they are boxes now.
5. Fix the comments:
   - :3039 "A box holds no tokens, so it never does": a box whose tokens need more than it holds is last, not a box.
   - The orders comment (:3031-3036) and `select_script_inputs`' doc: a box holding its pool's token is a box, weighed by what it adds.

WebAssembly (lib.rs):
1. Delete `ada_alone` (:4140-4144) and its filter (:4146), leaving `.filter(|&i| tier(&classes[i].1) == 2)`.
2. `total` is already the class's `adds.max(0)` summed, so the weights are right as they are.
3. Drop "those holding tokens after them" from :4137-4139.

Docs:
1. architecture.md:141 (order 3, "token-bearing ones included") should say that a token pool's way back is a box, weighed by what it adds.
2. The box order paragraph at :144 then holds as written.

Option 2, if the owner keeps boxes holding tokens after the ADA-only boxes:
1. Say so in architecture.md:144, privacy.md:173, privacy-policy.md:93 (the 18 November entry) and the histories.ts header (:23-27).
2. At least key a and b's tier 2 on `(box_rank(class) == 2, place)`, so a known token box sits ahead of every box of unknown making. That fixes case A but not case B.

This is the owner's question from the finding. Either way, add the two tests below.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on the branch's HEAD. I traced it from the way back's class through the worker into core and found nothing that catches it. I built and ran nothing.

1. A token pool's way back reaches selection as a mixed box that holds a token.
- wasm/src/lovejoin.rs, `WithdrawResult.token`: "A token pool's token, into the same register". The way back is one UTxO holding the box's ADA and its token.
- lovejoin.ts:8238 `mixedBoxOf(s, box) ? mixedBox(built.txHash)`. histories.ts `mixedBox` gives `{id: box:<tx>, origin: "mixed"}`, and wasm lib.rs:2158-2159 reads that as `Origin::Mixed`. `tier()` (build.rs:2549) puts it in tier 2.
- `spendable` (script-spend.ts:314-316) and coin control (coin-control.ts:290-293) take out only Seedelf tokens, reference scripts and the user's own locks.
- The Send goes lib.rs:3396 `transfer_apart(.., histories(Purpose::Pay, ..))`, then `select_script_inputs`, then `apart`, with floor = paid_out.

2. Core leaves it out of the box order.
- build.rs:3042 `let is_box = |u| tier(u) == 2 && !holds_tokens(u);` and :3043 `box_list` use only boxes of ADA alone. Only those get weights (:3045), a place (:3059-3070) or a more_mixed choice (:3142, :3166).
- Anything else gets `.unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` (:3069). In by_history (:3071) and by_tier (:3083), `place` comes before the rank, so a tier-2 UTxO holding tokens sorts after every ADA box, one of unknown making included.

3. Case A, traced.
- Step 1 skips every single UTxO: each is at or under the 16 ₳ floor.
- Step 2 builds nothing: every class has one row.
- Order a is [O, K, W, T]. O+K is 14.71 ₳ and is skipped; O+K+W builds.
- `more_mixed(weights, 2)` sees only K (rank 1) and W (rank 2), so j > mixed + others and it returns no choice.
- Result: O+K+W. O+K+T (18.86 ₳, about 2.4 ₳ of change carrying the token) pays with the same box count.

4. Case B: an 11 ₳ Send spends O+K1+K2 where O+T pays with one box.

5. The orders don't treat T alike. c's rest (`largest`, :3096) keeps T as ordinary money, so c with j = 0 is [O, T], while a and b put T after every box. The round meant one shared order.

6. Payments in parts do the same. lib.rs:4140-4147 keeps only `ada_alone` tier-2 classes in `boxes`, and :4169 gives every other class `usize::MAX`.

7. Nothing later catches it.
- historiesNote (histories.ts) says "2 boxes back from Lovejoin and money you made private" whichever box is merged.
- An unplaced box's `unknown:` part is left out of the Unknown count (`ofABox`), so the review never tells W from T, and there's no choice to make.
- Only the user locking W by hand on the UTxOs screen avoids it, and nothing prompts that.

8. The docs claim the rule with no exception for a box holding tokens:
- architecture.md:144: "a box someone else put in, its way back tagged Unknown, is never merged ahead of another box"
- privacy.md:173
- flows.md:377
- wasm/README.md:56
- privacy-policy.md:93: "A session's funding and a private payment, too, take a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of"

9. The fixer knew about the shift. round5.json, R5-code l4code#1 `left`: "tier-2 UTxOs holding tokens now come after the pure-ADA boxes". R5-docs still wrote the rule without the exception.

10. The impact.
- Who: nobody has to act. It hits an ordinary Send, Make public, funding or mint, for a user who holds a token pool's way back next to boxes of ADA alone. Mallory can supply W by depositing under a register copied from the Seedelf (it costs her the box), but she can't arrange T or the payment's size.
- Loss: no funds. In Case A, the planted box's way back ties the Send's inputs (O, so public account 0) and its recipient to the Seedelf whose register she copied, where T ties nothing. In Case B, two plain boxes are tied together where one mixed box paid, with a slightly higher fee.
- Reach is narrow today. A token return goes through a token pool only where one exists with enough boxes.
- Against 1.9.1, nobody is worse off. web-wallet/1.9.1 build.rs:2774-2782 had no Mixed origin and tied every box's rank, so `holds_tokens` put a token box after the ADA boxes then too.
- What's broken is round four's order at 1e1b0647 (T ranked ahead of K and W there) and the new docs and policy. Medium stands on the guide's "a claim wider than the code" and "a privacy link made by default".
verdicts.fix_notes:
This is the owner's call: either the code follows the docs, or the docs say what the code does.

Option A: code follows the rule.
1. In `apart`, build the box order over every tier-2 UTxO that isn't `last`: `in_order = tier(u) == 2 && !last(u)`. Leave a `last` one out: it would make `most` (boxes.len()) count something that sorts after everything.
2. Weigh each by what it adds: its ADA less its tokens' least. `apart` has no params, so have `select_script_inputs` compute an outpoint → `adds` map beside `piles` and pass it in. Rank each by `box_rank`, or 0 where `ties_nothing`.
3. Use that one list for `place`, `weights`, `more_mixed_built` and c's j prefix. Filter `largest` and `tokens_last` with the same predicate.
4. Careful: `more_mixed_built` gets `box_list` for every order, c included, and c's tail is `order[j..]` (c's rest, `grows = true`). The finding's "c's j prefix can stay ADA-only" with T in `box_list` lets a more-mixed choice pick T while c's rest still holds it. That puts the same input in twice and breaks the change arithmetic. So either take T out of c's rest, or give c an ADA-only list for its prefix and for its more_mixed_built.
5. Worth::apart (lib.rs:4146): drop `ada_alone`. Its weight is already `total`, which is adds-based.
6. Docs: architecture.md's box order should say that a box holding tokens is weighed by what it adds.

Option B, narrower.
- In a, b and Worth::apart, key tier 2 on (box of unknown making, place-or-MAX): a token box of known making goes before W, after the known ADA boxes.
- That fixes Case A, not Case B. The docs must then say that a box holding tokens comes after the boxes of ADA alone.

Option C: docs follow the code.
- Scope the rule to boxes of ADA alone in architecture.md:144, privacy.md:173, flows.md:377, wasm/README.md:56 and the policy's 18 November entry (:93).
- Say that a token pool's way back is merged after every box of ADA alone, one of unknown making included. That changes the policy's "take a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of".

Whichever is chosen, the extension sees a code change only after a WebAssembly rebuild.

findings.title: With a large box of unknown making and a UTxO holding a token, a spend that built at 1e1b0647 is now TooMany in every order: one payment goes in parts that merge 19 boxes, and several payments are refused
findings.scenario:
The private balance holds:
- U: 150 ₳ plus a token, made private (public:0)
- W: 199.7 ₳, box:w+unknown:w: the way back of a box from a pool of 200 ₳ boxes that the records don't place (after a restore, or via Bring every box back now)
- K1..K25: 4.71 ₳ boxes from the 5 ₳ pool
The user sends 300 ₳ to one Seedelf.
1. At 1e1b0647, order b (tier 2 by size, W first) builds U+W, as does order a when the K are plain. Two inputs.
2. Now:
   - Order a is [U, K1..K25, W]. U plus 21 K is 248.9 ₳ at 22 inputs, and the 23rd input is TooMany.
   - Order b is the same order, so it's skipped.
   - Order c with j up to 25 never reaches W, and j = 26 needs 27 inputs.
   - Order d is [W, K1..K25, U], tokens last. It reaches 298.6 ₳ at 22 inputs, then TooMany.
   - The result is Err(TooMany).
3. build_transfer_parts takes it to parts:
   - Worth::apart's order is U, K1..K25, W (boxes_to_merge: gap 150, j = 26, first = all).
   - Part 1 takes the first 20 (MAX_WITHDRAW_UTXOS): U with K1..K19.
   - Part 2 is W alone.
   - That's two transactions, U merged with 19 boxes, and about 1 ₳ more fee, where one transaction of U+W paid.
4. A Send to two Seedelfs at once is refused outright.
The window is any payment between W + 21 K and U + W, less fees (about 297 to 348 ₳ here). It needs both U and W above what 21 known boxes hold (about 99 ₳ for 5 ₳-pool boxes), so it's narrow.
findings.who: Nobody has to act. It needs a user with a box of unknown making from a pool of large boxes, many small known boxes, and a large private UTxO holding a token.
findings.evidence:
- build.rs:2576 `order.sort_by_key(|&i| (boxes[i].1 == 2, std::cmp::Reverse(boxes[i].0), boxes[i].1));` puts W after every known box in a and b (`place`) and in c (`boxes[..j]`, :3124-3131).
- :3133 d `(last(u), holds_tokens(u), std::cmp::Reverse(lovelace_of(u)))` puts U after every UTxO of ADA alone, so d can't rescue it.
- 1e1b0647:2958 `boxes.sort_by_key(|u| (!joins_base(u), std::cmp::Reverse(lovelace_of(u))));` and old by_tier's tier 2 by size reached [U, W].
- TooMany comes at the 23rd guessed spend (build.rs:1181-1192, :2085).
- lib.rs:5130 `Err(e) if too_much(&e) && request.payments.len() == 1 => e`, else `return Err(e)`. lib.rs:3564 `MAX_WITHDRAW_UTXOS: usize = 20`.
- round5.json's "so nothing new is refused" is true of more_mixed_built only. The reorder itself drops coverage.
findings.fix:
Keep the old coverage behind the round's orders. Just before d, chain c's orders once more with the boxes by size alone (1e1b0647's `(!joins_base, Reverse(lovelace))`), skipping a prefix already grown. It's reached only when a, b and c all failed, so no spend that builds today changes.

Test: the scenario above, scaled down, builds in one transaction.
findings.owner_question: Should a by-size fallback run before the CLI's order, so that nothing which built in one transaction before this round is now split or refused?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD (550a368f; the code is dc31711b). I traced it from the worker to core and found no guard the finder missed. Tests on a copy reproduce it, and the same tests pass with 1e1b0647's files swapped in. The tree was not touched.

**Classes**
- W is `unplacedBox` (histories.ts:84): id `box:<w>+unknown:<w>`. REACH (:151) gives it origin lovejoin, and lib.rs:2158 maps that to Origin::Lovejoin, so W is tier 2 (build.rs:2549).
- `box_rank` (build.rs:2561-2569) gives W 2, because the `unknown:` part doesn't start with `box:`. The K boxes get 0 (mixed) or 1 (plain).
- U is `public:0`, Own, tier 0. It holds a token, so it is not a box (:3042).

**Path**
transfer.ts:119 → lib.rs:5077 `build_transfer_parts` → `build_transfer` (:3439) → `transfer_spend` → `build::transfer_apart(.., Purpose::Pay ..)` → `apart`. Each attempt is `paying` plus `estimate()`. The guess is 450M steps per input (:1189) against a 10B limit (:1181), so `settle` (:2085) returns TooMany past 22 inputs.

**What `apart` tries**
- Steps 1 to 3 find nothing:
  - Every single UTxO is at or below the floor, so it is Skipped (:2937).
  - Every class has one row.
  - No tokens are sent.
- Order a. `boxes_largest_first` (:2576) sorts by `(rank == 2, Reverse(size), rank)`, so `boxes` is [K1..K25, W]. `place` (:3065) puts that order into a and b, so a is [U, K1..K25, W].
  - Every prefix up to [U, K1..K25] (267.75 ₳) is Skipped.
  - The first prefix tried is all 27 inputs, which is TooMany.
  - The finder's "23rd input" detail is off for a; the outcome is the same.
- Order b is the same order, so it is skipped as grown before (:3155).
- Order c, j = 1..25 ([Kj.., U]), is short. j = 26 fails at 26 boxes, which sets `boxes_fail`.
- Order d (:3133) is [W, K1..K25, U]. W plus 22 K is 23 inputs: TooMany.
- The result is Err(TooMany).
- At 1e1b0647, the boxes went by size (:2958). Order b was [U, W, ..] and built U + W, and so did order a when the K boxes were plain.

**Parts**
- lib.rs:5130: `Err(e) if too_much(&e) && request.payments.len() == 1`. Anything else is returned as an error.
- `Worth::apart` → `boxes_to_merge`. The gap is about 151 ₳, so j = 26 and `more_mixed` returns nothing (25 < 26). The order is U, K.., W.
- `in_parts` takes the top 20 (`Room::new`, MAX_WITHDRAW_UTXOS = 20). The rest goes as an amount, which W pays alone.

**Measured (WebAssembly test)**

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds, at low severity. I traced it on HEAD (550a368f) and found no guard that stops it.

**The trace** (extension/src/background/lovejoin.ts):
1. Restore read. owned = [F, U]. No due times, no origins.
   - In `moreThanDue` (:2164), `held` (:2168) is notMixedYet (:2129, depositsOf by origins) plus bootstrapOf.
   - `mixedFor(undefined)` gives undefined, not false (:1272), so neither box is held. back = 2 against due 0, and :2183 `return back > dueIn(s, p).length - theirDue;` is true.
   - `found()` (:6492) asks about [F, U]. Koios answers F as a mix; U goes into `asking`.
   - sortOut holds U as unsure (:6317, :6323 `...deposits, ...unsure`, :6325), so `free` = [F].
   - status (:6830) runs scheduleFound with `back` = free only (:5789). That draws one due time, F's. U gets none.
2. Someone else's mix moves F to M3. Due times are per pool, not per box, so F's stays. No squareUp entry or ended chain removes it.
3. Next read. owned = [M3, U]. `rejudge` (:6638) skips both: it works only on kept origins, and `blind` is depositsOf, which is empty here.
   - `moreThanDue` holds neither box, so back = 2 against due 1, and the count is over. `found()` returns every unknown box, so one tx_info is sent for [M3, U].
4. Bring one back anyway's press: `force` stays empty when `anyway` is set (:7523). Its sortOut (:7532) goes through the same `found`, so it sends [M3, U] too.

**Guards I checked, none of which stops it:**
- `rejudge` leaves U and M3 alone.
- found's asking-only branch runs only when the count is not over.
- `covered()`/inputsOf: on mainnet the data layer answers for a pool it lists, so no Koios request goes there. But U waits only where Koios answers: preprod, Koios-only, the data layer down, or a later pool of the same box value, which ours doesn't cover.
- Retired pools have no sweep: an unsure box there is free and gets a due time. So the sweep is in current pools only.

**The words:**
- Policy :28 says "again at each later pool read that counts your boxes (...), about one the Cardano server hasn't answered for yet, until it answers".
- :44 says the same: "...**Bring one back anyway**'s included, about one it hasn't answered for yet, until it does".
- :93's list repeats it. Its last clause is narrower still: "before **Bring one back anyway** takes it ... only at the pool read before each, about one the server hasn't answered for yet". Run 3 below shows that read also sends M3.
- "other boxes" appears in the policy only in the 1.9.1 sentence ("together with that pool's other boxes of yours the wallet has no record or answer for"). Set against the general clause, that implies the general re-ask doesn't sweep.
- The entry claims to say "exactly when".
- privacy.md:475 says the sweep outright: "While its box is held for that answer, with no due time, each such read asks about the pool's other boxes no record or answer names too, together". architecture.md:717 does too. round5.json's R5-docs policy_facts confirm the restore-case form went to privacy.md only.

**The best refutation, and why it fails:** the first clause, "at a pool read that finds more of your boxes than it expects ... about all such boxes together", covers the sweep if "expects" means "has due times for". The policy never says so. In the scenario the read finds the same count as before (M3 in F's place), so a reader would expect only U to be asked.

**Run in a copy** (test below):
- U waiting: the next read sends [[M3, U]] (due 1 after the restore read).
- Control, with U answered as a deposit (also held, with no due time): the same move asks nothing. So the sweep comes from the unsure box alone.
- Bring one back anyway's press while N waits sends [[M3, N]].
- The words check fails at all three places.
- tests/r5-when-it-asks.test.ts passes 4/4.

**Why low:**
- Nobody can cause it. It needs a restore, plus Koios not answering one transaction, plus another mixer's mix moving one of the wallet's boxes in that pool during that window.
- The cost is small. Koios gets M3 grouped with U in one request, sooner than M3's own lone ask before its withdraw. Both come from the IP address Koios sees anyway.
- The policy's first clause literally covers it, but the 1.9.1 contrast and the "only" at :93 read narrower than the code.

Same rating as round four's l4docs#2 (the 1.9.1 case of this count). One overstatement in the finding: "A steady wallet never asks about M3 at a pool read" holds for the move alone. A steady wallet whose count goes over for another reason (a stranger's deposit) sweeps M3 too, which the first clause covers.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD. I traced every path end to end and found no guard the finder missed. Three tests fail exactly where the words and the code part ways.

**What the words say.**
- Policy :28 says the wallet asks "again at each later pool read that counts your boxes (opening Lovejoin's page, or pressing a **Bring one back** button, say), about one the Cardano server hasn't answered for yet, until it answers". The same line later says "the pool read before each asks again about any box the Cardano server hasn't answered for yet".
- Policy :44 first lists the asks before Mix my boxes again, before a box comes back by itself, and at Bring one back now / Bring one back. Only then does it add "and again at each later pool read that counts your boxes, **Bring one back anyway**'s included, about one it hasn't answered for yet, until it does". Placed after the whole list, that reads as a rule over every ask.
- Policy :93 says "It also says exactly when … again at each later pool read that counts your boxes about one the Cardano server hasn't answered for yet".
- privacy.md:475 says "Each transaction is asked about once and the answer kept; one Koios doesn't answer for is asked again at every pool read that counts the boxes until it does". privacy.md :253 and :460 say the same.

**What the code does.** The only standing re-ask is the `asking` record.
- `found` (lovejoin.ts:6492): `moreThanDue(...) ? theirs : theirs.filter((b) => s.asking?.[b.txHash] !== undefined)`. While the count holds, only boxes already in `asking` are counted.
- :6494 `holding` is the counted boxes. The ask is `holding` plus `force`, and :6498 calls `lookUp(network, ask, holding)`.
- :6548 `const silent = asked.filter((tx) => !told.has(tx) && holding.has(tx));` and :6554 `for (const tx of silent) asking[tx] ??= at;`. Only boxes in `holding` that got no answer are kept.
- `made` (:6519) calls `this.lookUp(network, ask, new Set())`, so nothing it asks is kept. Its own doc (:6505-6512) says a silent one "isn't kept as still asked of".
- Forced boxes from `withdrawNowNow` (:7523 `force = [chosen]`, :7530 `force = first < 0 ? ranked : ranked.slice(0, first)`) are not in `holding`. Unanswered, they come back as `untold` and are not kept.
- At a due time (:7384-7385), `made([box])` comes back untold. The due time moves to a fresh draw within `WITHDRAW_SPREAD_MS` (5 to 60 minutes, :1768) and the run returns.
- A Koios failure is a silent answer, not a throw: `inputsOf` (:6712-6718) catches a `KoiosError` and breaks, and a read timeout or a 500 is a `KoiosError` (koios.ts:1388).
- Only two places add to `asking`: :6554 (boxes in `holding`) and `rejudge` :6674 (the 1.9.1 once-more ask). `sortOut` :6419 only removes entries.
- Bring every box back now (`bringAllBackNow`, :7753) reads with `ours` (:3582) and never calls `sortOut` or `found`. `split` (:7988), `splitAll` (:8010) and `rooms` (:3715) don't either. One small slip in the finding: `rooms` counts only other people's boxes, not the wallet's.

**The finder's scenario, step by step.** On preprod in a steady state, M takes over B's due time, so the count holds. At M's due time, `made` asks Koios about M, Koios fails, and M gets a fresh draw. M is not put in `asking`. When the Lovejoin page then reads the pool (`status`, then `sortOut`, then `found`), nothing is asked.

**The narrow behaviour is deliberate.**
- lovejoin-restore.test.ts:1069 asserts that `asking` is still undefined after a due run's failed ask ("nothing is kept for the pool reads"). I re-ran it at HEAD in the copy and it passes.
- architecture.md:717 already states this exactly: "(a failed lookup there isn't kept)", and Bring every box back now reads "with `ours`, never `sortOut`".
- Only the policy and privacy.md widen it to every box the server hasn't answered for.

**Severity: low.** The rubric lists "a claim wider than the code" under medium. I keep this at low for three reasons:
- The words err on the safe side. They disclose more Koios asks than happen; no ask goes unmentioned and no link is made.
- It only matters after Koios fails to answer: on preprod, with Koios-only on, with the data layer down, or for a later pool of the same box value.
- Each such box is still asked again at its next due time or press, which the clauses "before it comes back by itself" and "when you press" already cover. So "until it answers" stays true; only "at each pool read" is too wide.

Because :93 says "exactly when", the lead may want to raise it to medium.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 550a368f, both parts, end to end. Failing tests confirm each claim. I found no guard the finder missed.

How the classes get there. A box of unknown making is `unplacedBox` = merged([boxFrom, unknownIn]) (histories.ts:90). That gives id `box:<w>+unknown:<w>` with origin "lovejoin", since REACH lists lovejoin before unknown. In core that is tier 2 (build.rs `tier`) and box_rank 2 (build.rs:2561). A token pool's way back is classed by the same withdrawOne code for every pool: lovejoin.ts:8238-8244 uses `mixedBoxOf(s, box) ? mixedBox(..)`, and mixedBoxOf (lovejoin.ts:2467) is per pool. activity.ts:386 says "A box back from Lovejoin brings its pool's token in with its ADA (a token pool's, chunk 34)". classOf keeps the stored class (lovejoin-withdraw is not in LEAVES_CHANGE). readContract passes those UTxOs to selection through coins.seedelf, with no token filter. privacy.md:405 itself calls a token pool's box a box: "boxes of one value: ADA alone, or a set amount of one token and of ADA".

(a) "So it spends as few boxes as pay" (architecture.md:144) is false.
- build.rs:2576 `order.sort_by_key(|&i| (boxes[i].1 == 2, std::cmp::Reverse(boxes[i].0), boxes[i].1));` puts rank 2 after every known box, whatever its size.
- build.rs:2594 makes more_mixed return nothing once j passes the known boxes.
- With only boxes, `largest` is empty, so order c (fewest_boxes) doesn't run. Order a builds first.
- Test: five mixed boxes of 4.71 ₳ and W of 24.71 ₳, 26 ₳ out. Send, Make public and a funding each spend 6 boxes, where W plus one other pays (checked with transfer_from / sweep_many_from plus estimate).
- The round's own pin, a_box_of_unknown_making_is_merged_after_every_other_box, says "takes all three ... where by size alone W and one other paid".
- The parts do the same: Worth::apart gives [51,52,53,54,55,70].
- The same unscoped "as few as pay" is in privacy.md:173, flows.md:377 and wasm/README.md:56.

(b) "after every other box" and the policy's "take a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of" fail for a token pool's way back.
- build.rs:3042 `let is_box = |u| tier(u) == 2 && !holds_tokens(u);` leaves token holders out of the box order. They get `.unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` (3069), so by_history and by_tier (sorted by tier, then place) put every ADA box, Unknown ones included, ahead of them.
- Test: K plain 4.71 ₳, W unknown 9.71 ₳, X a mixed token-pool way back of 9.71 ₳ plus a token. With 12 ₳ out, Send, Make public and a funding all spend K+W, never X, although K+X pays.
- WebAssembly does the same: lib.rs:4146 `ada_alone` filter and :4169 `unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` give [41, 30, 60].
- Order c: `largest` and `tokens_last` (3096, 3106) filter `!is_box`. So token boxes of any making sit among "every other UTxO" at j = 0, and architecture.md:141's "the rest of the boxes left out" is false for them. This is reachable only after orders a and b fail, so I didn't test it.
- The code's comment at build.rs:3039, "A box holds no tokens", states the same wrong assumption.

Beyond the finding, same root, step 1:
- MAX_TOKEN_SINGLES (12) counts token-bearing candidates even when they are Skipped (one_more, build.rs:2840-2846).
- Twelve token bundles made private (Own, rank 0 for Pay) use up the 12 tries. X, a mixed token-pool box that pays alone, is then never tried, and W (ADA, rank 5) is taken alone.
- Test: spent W where X was expected. That also breaks privacy.md:173's "one the wallet knows is mixed before any other where one pays alone" and policy :93.

What holds:
- The ADA-alone order works as built: the existing apart tests all pass in the copy.
- The hatch's private payer takes only ADA alone (wasm lovejoin.rs:2969), so the policy's hatch clause is true, and "of ADA alone" fits it.

Why low: this matches l4docs#3, the same claim failing in fallback orders, which was rated low. It needs a token pool's way back plus a box tagged Unknown, with a merge where either would pay, or 12+ token UTxOs ranked ahead. The cost is a box someone else may have put in being merged where a mixed one would do. No funds are at risk. Read strictly as "a claim wider than the code" in the published policy, it could be argued medium.

findings.title: A page that reloads in a signature's unlock wait is still spared by another tab's enable(), so every reload re-focuses the window and the site never waits (the mirror of l4code#3)
findings.scenario:
1. Any https site; the wallet is locked. Its tab B calls enable(). unlocked() pushes an enable waiter and shows the window, and B stays in `enabling` while it waits.
2. Its tab A posts signData and waits for the unlock too. A page can post it without enable(): bridge.ts:93 relays any dApp method. Then tab A reloads.
3. gone(A) finds no connect question and one unlock wait. sharedBeyond(A) is true because of B, so the site is only marked spared, with no `question`, and refuseFor never runs.
4. The reloaded page's signData meets no refusal in unlocked() (:1659) and calls window.show() (:1678). That focuses the open window with drawAttention (dapp-window.ts:24). The site can repeat this every reload.
5. No decline ever lands. The unlock deletes a mark that has no question (:795), and B's enable() ending deletes it too (:620-624).

The same happens in two more cases:
- A connected site. After the unlock, B's enable() returns at :1187-1190, before any refusal check, and asks no connect question. So the stated reason for sparing ("which asks itself and a refusal would turn away", architecture.md:565) doesn't hold.
- A connected private-session site whose B enable() sits in funded() for up to FUNDING_WAIT_MS (20 min).

Round five's new dapp-gone case pins only the opposite pairing: a page reloaded in its enable()'s unlock wait beside a signature's wait is turned away after one show.
findings.who: Any https page that opens two tabs of its own while the wallet is locked. The user's only ways out are closing the window, which refuses the site, or unlocking.
findings.evidence:
dapp.ts:989-992: `private sharedBeyond(session) { const live = (id) => id !== session.id && !this.gonePages.has(id); return [...(this.enabling.get(session.origin)?.keys() ?? [])].some(live); }`. Any running enable() counts, whatever it waits on.
dapp.ts:966: `if (!this.sharedBeyond(session)) this.refuseFor(...)`, else only `this.spared.set(...)`.
dapp.ts:1659: `if (this.refusing(origin) && (method !== "enable" || !known))`. With the site spared, nothing refuses the next page's signData.
dapp.ts:1678: `await this.deps.window.show();`. dapp-window.ts:24: `chrome.windows.update(open.windowId, { focused: true, drawAttention: true })`.
dapp.ts:795: `if (!this.spared.get(u.session.origin)?.question) this.spared.delete(u.session.origin);`.
dapp.ts:621-623: `this.enabling.delete(session.origin); … this.spared.delete(session.origin);`.
dapp.ts:225: `FUNDING_WAIT_MS = 20 * 60_000`.
The brief's B7: "Only another page waiting on the same connect question spares a site". G6's harm was a page re-opening the focused window as often as it reloads.
The new test 'a page reloaded in its enable()'s unlock wait brings the window back once, then waits' parks a signData and reloads enable(). No case parks an enable() and reloads a signData.
findings.fix:
Keep B's enable() asked, but give the reloading page the back-off.
- In gone(): when the leaving page had no connect question and none of its unlock waits was an enable() (`unlocking.every((u) => !u.enable)`), record a short signatures-only refusal even when sharedBeyond is true.
- unlocked() applies that refusal to `method !== "enable"`: NOT_CONNECTED, no window. enable() ignores it, so the waiting enable() is still asked.
- Narrower alternative: leave out of sharedBeyond an enable() that will ask no connect question, i.e. a site `lastSites` knows is connected, or one already in funded().

Test, in dapp-gone's l4code#3 describe:
- Lock the wallet and leave a page's enable() waiting.
- Four times: a new page's signData, then gone() once the window shows.
- Expect ["window shown", NOT_CONNECTED, NOT_CONNECTED, NOT_CONNECTED]; HEAD gives "window shown" four times.
- After the unlock, the enable()'s connect question is still asked.
findings.owner_question: Should a page that leaves a signature's or a send's unlock wait meet the back-off even while another tab's enable() waits for the unlock, as long as that enable() is still asked? Or is a waiting enable() enough to spare the site, as the policy's "unless another of its pages is asking to connect too" allows?

verdicts.evidence:
The mechanism is real on HEAD 550a368f. It is still not a defect: the code follows the rule as the policy and the docs state it, and the harm doesn't depend on it, because another path B7 spares on purpose gives the site the same result. I traced it end to end and ran it in a copy of the tree (now deleted). The fixes tree is untouched and clean.

**What holds (traced, then tested)**
- Any https page can post signData without enable(). bridge.ts:89-97 `relay` forwards any `isDappMethod`. sw.ts:394-434 gives each port its own `crypto.randomUUID()` session (sw.ts:370), so a reload is a new page, and `onDisconnect` calls `dapp.gone(session)` (sw.ts:435).
- Tab B's enable() while locked: `countEnabling(B, 1)` (dapp.ts:593), then unlocked() pushes `{enable: true}` and shows the window (:1671-1678).
- Tab A's signData: unlocked() finds no refusal (:1659), pushes its own waiter and calls `await this.deps.window.show()` (:1678). That runs `chrome.windows.update(open.windowId, { focused: true, drawAttention: true })` (dapp-window.ts:24).
- gone(A): there is no question, and `unlocking.length` is 1 (:961-962). `sharedBeyond(A)` returns `[...(this.enabling.get(session.origin)?.keys() ?? [])].some(live)` (:989-992), which is true because of B, so only `spared.set` runs (:967-972) and refuseFor never does.
- No other guard exists: nothing throttles show(), and gone() frees A's place (MAX_SITE_WAITING, :1668).
- The test's 'the finding' case gives `["window shown" ×4]` where the finder expects one show, then NOT_CONNECTED. Its connected-site variant gives the same. Both fail on HEAD in the default build and with VITE_ENABLE_MAINNET=false.
- The control, a signature reloaded with no other tab, gives `["window shown", NOT_CONNECTED ×3]`.

**Why it isn't a defect**
1. **The code says what the words say.**
   - Policy :93: "A site whose page goes away before you answer its connect question, or its wait for the unlock (a reload, say), now has to wait …, unless another of its pages is asking to connect too." Policy :29 and privacy.md:350 say the same.
   - architecture.md:565: "unless another page of the same site has an `enable()` running, waiting on that question, on the unlock before it …".
   - B is asking to connect, so the leaving page's method doesn't matter. Round five's lead approved this wording as B7 (round5.json, l4docs#4). B is on its way to the site's one connect question. That is not the l4code#3 shape, where the page doing the sparing would never ask one.
2. **The harm is reachable without this path, and the sketch leaves it open.**
   - Test 'B7's own pairing': with the same enable() of B waiting, a page reloaded in its own enable()'s wait gives `["window shown" ×4]` on HEAD. It shares B's place (`shares`, :1667) and calls show() each time, while gone() spares it.
   - dapp-gone's 'nor when another page's enable() of the same site still waits for the unlock' pins exactly this sparing.
   - I applied the finder's sketch in the copy: a signatures-only refusal set in gone() when `!question && unlocking.every((u) => !u.enable)`, and refused for `method !== "enable"` in unlocked(). The finding's two cases then pass, and dapp-gone passes all 26 cases.
   - But 'B7's own pairing' still gives four shows. A site that wants the window back just reloads with enable() instead. So the sketch changes which call the site makes, not what it can do.
3. **The connected-site cases add nothing.**
   - A connected site's enable() while locked is never refused: `if (this.refusing(origin) && (method !== "enable" || !known))` (:1659), by design, so as not to reveal the lock (L36).
   - Test 'a connected site alone' gives `["window shown" ×4]` with no second tab and nothing spared, even though gone() runs refuseFor each time.
   - The same goes for the private-session funded() case (:1189, :1474-1501), since that site is connected too.

**Residual nit, internal docs only**
- architecture.md:565 gives the reason for sparing as "which asks itself and a refusal would turn away".
- That is not true of a connected site's enable() that asks for no governance. It returns at dapp.ts:1187-1190, before the refusing() check at :1216.
- The rule as stated is right. No harm follows from the imprecise reason.

**Minor point**
The finding's "No decline ever lands" holds only while B stays until the unlock. If B leaves while locked, `gone(B)` → `sharedBeyond(B)` is false → refuseFor, so the decline lands then.
verdicts.fix_notes:
No code change, and don't apply the sketch.
- The sketch works as written: simulated in a copy, the finding's cases pass and dapp-gone stays at 26 of 26.
- It closes nothing, though. The same window comes back on every reload when the reloading page calls enable() beside the same waiting enable(). That pairing is B7's own exception, pinned in dapp-gone.test.ts.
- For a connected site, enable() reloads bring the window back with no second tab at all (dapp.ts:1659, L36).

The owner question can be answered from the record: a waiting enable() is enough to spare the site. That is what the policy's dApps row, its 18 November entry, privacy.md:350 and architecture.md:565 already say ("unless another of its pages is asking to connect too").

If the owner wants a reload loop closed whichever call the page makes, that is a new call against B7's exception, not this finding's fix. For example, unlocked() could skip `window.show()` for a page whose site already has a waiter in `unlocking`, since the window is already showing that site's unlock. Decide it with the owner, because it also changes the existing enable()+enable() and connected-site behaviour.

Optional nit, architecture.md:565: "which asks itself and a refusal would turn away" could read "which, for a site not yet connected (or one asking for governance), asks itself, and a refusal would turn it away". That makes the reason exact for a connected site's enable(), which returns at dapp.ts:1187-1190 before the refusal check at :1216. This is wording only; the policy and privacy.md need nothing.

findings.title: Merge order c's same-count swap regrows the rest, so it can trade a plain box for a mixed one by merging more of the other UTxOs (more payers tied, more fee)
findings.scenario:
1. The private balance holds 25 payments received of 2 ₳ each, each its own class. It also holds L, a plain way back from 1.9.1 (9.71 ₳), and X, a mixed one (4.71 ₳).
2. The user makes a Make public or Send of 43 ₳. Steps 1 and 2 pay nothing.
3. Orders a and b reach the 23rd payment, past what one transaction spends, before any box. c with j = 0 repeats a's prefix and is skipped.
4. c with j = 1 builds L plus about 18 payments: 19 inputs.
5. more_mixed_built then swaps X in and grows the payments again from scratch. X plus 20 payments is short, so it returns X plus 21 payments (22 inputs), where that still fits the limit.

The box count is the same, but three more payers' payments are merged into one transaction, at about 0.036 ₳ more fee per extra Seedelf input. That is the cost l4code#1 was fixed to avoid: one more history merged, and more fee. Orders a and b can't do this, because their swap has an empty tail and so exactly the same inputs. Only c's swap (`grows: true`) regrows. No test sees it: the guard past_the_input_limit_one_box_still_pays_where_the_mixed_one_falls_short (47 ₳) has the regrowth hit TooMany, so L is kept.
findings.who: Nobody acts. It takes an ordinary Send, Make public or funding from a balance with more small UTxOs than one transaction spends, beside a plain box and a smaller mixed one.
findings.evidence:
build.rs:3129, c's orders: `(order, j, Some((0, j, true)))`.
build.rs:3162-3166: `let with = k.saturating_sub(from).min(most); let tail = if grows { &order[from + most..] } else { &[] }; … more_mixed_built(&order[..from], with, tail, weighed, &mut try_with)`.
build.rs:2903: `match grow(&order, head.len() + j, try_with)`. It grows over the whole tail and isn't capped at the k it replaces.
build.rs:3024-3025, c's comment: "so no more boxes are spent together than pay. For each j, the rest the largest first, tokens or not, for the fewest inputs".
round5.json R5-code: "c's other inputs are regrown for it".
findings.fix:
Cap the swap at the input count of the build it replaces.
- Pass more_mixed_built the k it built with, and grow `order[..head.len() + k - from]`: for c, the chosen j boxes and the first k − j of the rest.
- A mixed box is then swapped in only where it pays with no more inputs. Orders a and b are unchanged.
- If the owner prefers the regrowth, pin it instead and drop "for the fewest inputs" from c's comment.

Test, in mint_test.rs mod apart:
- 25 received of 2 ₳, L plain 9.71 ₳, X mixed 4.71 ₳, a 43 ₳ Make public and a Send.
- Expect no more inputs than L's build: L spent, X not.
findings.owner_question: Among choices with as many boxes, should a box a mix moved win even where it needs more of the other UTxOs (more payments merged, more fee), or only where it pays with the same number of inputs?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 550a368f. The tree's build.rs and mint_test.rs match HEAD. A failing test reproduces it for a Send, a Make public and a funding. I found no guard the finder missed.

The path, traced end to end:
- **The real Send reaches it.** transfer.ts:92 `readContract` hands every Seedelf UTxO and its class to `wasm.buildTransferParts` (:119). lib.rs:5128-5131 `build_transfer_parts` tries one `build_transfer` first. That calls `build::transfer_apart` with `Purpose::Pay` (lib.rs:3396), then `select_script_inputs`, then `apart`.
- **Steps 1 and 2 pay nothing.** No single UTxO pays 43 ₳ (:2967), and every class holds one UTxO (:2988).
- **Order a fails.** Its order is the 25 payments, then L, then X (:3072-3082). 22 payments are short, and the 23rd is `TooMany`: `Failed`, kept in `grown`.
- **b and c with j = 0 are skipped.** b sorts the same as a, and c with j = 0 is a's prefix. Both are skipped at :3153-3156.
- **c with j = 1 builds L and 18 payments.** Its order is `(order, j, Some((0, j, true)))` (:3129), and `grow` builds at k = 19.
- **The swap regrows.** :3163-3164 gives `with` = min(k, j) = j and `tail = &order[from + most..]`, which is every non-box UTxO in c's rest. `more_mixed_built` (:2896-2906) builds `chosen ++ tail` and runs `grow(&order, head.len() + j, try_with)` (:2903). That starts at j and grows over the whole tail, with no cap at k.
- **The swap only ever adds inputs.** `boxes_largest_first`'s first j are the j largest boxes whose making is known. Any choice with more mixed boxes sums to no more, so it needs as many of the rest or more.
- **Orders a and b can't regrow.** Their swap is `(ahead, boxes.len(), false)` (:3142) with an empty tail. It tries exactly the head (every tier-0/1 UTxO) plus the chosen boxes: k inputs. c is the only order with part of its rest left out, so it is the only one that can regrow.

Measured on HEAD's code (estimate fees):
- **L case.** L and 18 payments: 19 inputs, fee 1,064,306. X with 20 is short, X with 21 builds (22 inputs, fee 1,201,126), and X with 22 is `TooMany`. All three spends take X and 21 payments: 3 more payers tied and 136,820 lovelace more fee, about 0.046 ₳ per input (the finding said about 0.036).
- **The cost grows with the size gap.** P is a merged way back `box:<a>+box:<b>` of 19.42 ₳, origin lovejoin, box_rank 1. P and 13 payments pay: 14 inputs, fee 836,270. All three spends take X and 21 instead: 8 more payers and 364,856 lovelace more.
- **No test sees it.** With a cap applied in the copy, every seedelf-core binary passes (mint_test 66, the new test included). So does every native seedelf-wasm binary, except lovejoin_proven_bytes_test, which reads seedelf-verification outside the copy. Nothing in the suite pins the regrowth.

Two small inaccuracies in the finding, neither of which changes it:
- b never runs: it is skipped as a's own order.
- The fee per extra input is nearer 0.046 ₳ at the estimate's guessed budget.

Why low and not medium:
- The code follows the lead's rule as written ("among choices of the same count, the one with a box a mix moved"). R5-code chose the regrowth on purpose (round5.json: "c's other inputs are regrown for it").
- The docs say "as many" boxes (architecture.md:144 "the choice of as many with the most boxes marked mixed that pays too", privacy.md:173 "among as many"), so no doc is false.
- The tension is with c's own comment (:3024-3025 "for the fewest inputs") and privacy.md:173's "tries not to merge histories".
- It is a trade, not a pure loss: X ties nothing, while L "may still tie to whatever paid for it" (Origin::Lovejoin's doc). The review's merge note shows what goes together.

This is the owner's call.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Ask the owner first: the finding's owner_question. Both answers have a cost.
- With the regrowth, a mixed box can pull in up to as many more payments as fit under the input limit. That was 3 beside L and 8 beside a 19.42 ₳ merged way back.
- With a cap, a near-tie goes to the plain box. If X is a few hundred lovelace smaller than L and X with the same count falls short by that much, L is kept where the regrowth would take X and one more payment.
- A middle ground, at most one input more than the build it replaces, covers the near-tie. Use it only if the owner asks.

**If the owner picks "only with the same number of inputs":**
- **The code.** One line, build.rs:3164:
  `let tail: &[&UtxoResponse] = if grows { &order[from + most..k.max(from + most)] } else { &[] };`
  c's swap then grows the chosen boxes plus at most k − j of its rest, so it never spends more than k inputs. Orders a and b are unchanged, since their tail is empty. I ran this exact line in the copy: the new test passes (19 and 14 inputs, L and P spent, X not), and every seedelf-core binary and native seedelf-wasm binary passes.
- **Comments.**
  - :3139-3141: "whether what follows them grows after that choice too (c's rest)" becomes "up to as many inputs as it built with".
  - more_mixed_built's doc (:2886-2888): "then `tail` one at a time" becomes "up to as many inputs".
  - c's comment (:3034-3036): "where it builds" becomes "where it builds with as many inputs".
- **Docs.**
  - architecture.md:144: "where that pays, the choice of as many with the most boxes marked mixed that pays too" gains "with no more inputs".
  - privacy.md:173 and flows.md:377 "among as many" become, for example, "among as many, where it takes no more of your other money".
  - Re-run R5-docs's check_words5.py if it pins those words.
- **The test.** Add the one under Test to mint_test.rs mod apart.

**If the owner keeps the regrowth:**
- Pin it with the same test reversed: X spent, L and P not, 22 inputs.
- c's comment at :3024-3025, "for the fewest inputs", should then say the fewest for the boxes chosen, and that a choice with more mixed boxes may take more of the rest.
- architecture.md:144 and privacy.md:173 should say so too, for example "even where it takes more of your other money".

No WebAssembly change either way. Worth::apart's `boxes_to_merge` covers the same gap with as many boxes, and every other history is in already, so it never regrows.

findings.scenario:
1. The private balance holds P, a 1.9.1 plain way back (`box:

In step 1's key, break the Lovejoin tie by box_rank for tier-2 classes: `(last(u), purpose.rank(&class(u)), if tier(u) == 2 { box_rank(&class(u)) } else { 0 })`, then size.

Test, in mint_test.rs mod apart:
- P plain at BOX + 300, W `box:<w>+unknown:<w>` at BOX.
- A 9 ₳ Send, a funding and a stealth mint each spend P alone.
findings.owner_question: Should one box that pays alone take a plain box before one of unknown making, as merging and the escape hatch now do, or is size order accepted there?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 550a368f. I found no guard the finder missed. I ran it, and on HEAD the smaller of P and W is spent for every purpose. Two corrections: the finder's numbers never reach step 1, and the behaviour is a gap, not a breach of any stated rule.

The path, traced end to end:
- **Classes.** `unplacedBox(tx)` = `merged([boxFrom(tx), unknownIn(tx)])` (histories.ts:91). `originOfAll` takes the first REACH entry present (["session","own","received","lovejoin","unknown"]), so W is `{id: "box:<w>+unknown:<w>", origin: "lovejoin"}`. withdrawOne seals that for a box it can't place, Bring every box back now included, since it asks nothing (lovejoin.ts:8250-8256). With no private payer, `besides` is empty and `origin = own`.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 550a368f. I traced it end to end and found no guard the finder missed. A test fails on HEAD for all 9 spends it tries. The code does what the lead decided. The docs that round five wrote claim more than the code does.

How the path runs
1. Classes.
   - A way back the wallet can't place gets `unplacedBox` (lovejoin.ts:8244). histories.ts:90 makes that `merged([boxFrom(txHash), unknownIn(txHash)])`: id `box:<w>+unknown:<w>`, origin lovejoin.
   - Known boxes are `boxFrom` (plain) or `mixedBox`. lib.rs:2153-2160 maps the origin strings to core's Origin.
2. Nothing filters W out.
   - readContract (script-spend.ts:239-246) passes every free UTxO with its class.
   - spendable (:314-316) drops only Seedelf tokens and reference scripts.
3. Into core.
   - A Send goes through transfer_apart with Purpose::Pay (lib.rs:3396-3399). A funding or a Make public goes through sweep_many_apart with Fund or Pay (lib.rs:3830-3835).
   - Both call select_script_inputs with floor = paid_out, then apart.
4. In apart.
   - Steps 1 and 2 pay nothing. Each single box is at or under the floor, so it is Skipped (build.rs:2937). Each box is a class of its own.
   - box_rank (build.rs:2561-2569) gives W rank 2.
   - boxes_largest_first sorts by `(boxes[i].1 == 2, Reverse(lovelace), rank)` (:2576). The order is B1, B2, W.
   - Order a grows B1 (Skipped), then B1+B2 at 9.42 ₳ (Skipped), then B1+B2+W, which builds.
   - more_mixed returns nothing once j reaches W (:2594 `if j > mixed.len() + others.len()`).
   - Order c is dropped when the balance is all boxes (:3125 `.filter(|_| !largest.is_empty())`), and it uses the same box order anyway.
   - Only order d, the CLI's order (W first), would spend W plus one box. It is never reached once a builds (:3168).

The run, in a copy under the memory cap
- All 9 spends took 3 boxes with W among them: the funding, the Make public and the Send, each with the other two boxes plain, one mixed, or both mixed.
- W plus one other box pays each of them. That costs 45,608 lovelace less fee: for example 334,594 against 288,986 for the Send.
- The existing pin `a_box_of_unknown_making_is_merged_after_every_other_box` passes. It pins this on purpose: mint_test.rs:3746-3749 says "12 ₳ out takes all three, W last, where by size alone W and one other paid".

Where the docs say more than the code (round five, f697c355)
- privacy.md:173 says "as few as pay, the largest first: among as many, one the wallet knows is mixed first, and one tagged Unknown too after every other box". Before round five it said "one at a time".
- flows.md:377 says the same.
- wasm/README.md:56 says the same (the finder missed this one).
- architecture.md:144 ends with "So it spends as few boxes as pay". Before round five that sentence covered only order 3. Now it covers the whole box order, the Unknown rule included.
- R5-code's policy_facts[0] said "even where that merges more boxes". The docs dropped it.

Code comments with the same overclaim
- build.rs:2571-2573 (boxes_largest_first): "so no more are spent together than pay". The finder missed this one.
- build.rs:2604-2607 (boxes_to_merge): "the fewest that add more than `gap`". The finder missed this one.
- build.rs:3022-3024 (order c): "so no more boxes are spent together than pay".
- build.rs:2737-2738: "so two are spent together only when nothing else pays". l4code#1's impact verdict already said to drop it.
- build.rs:2472, 2487, 2501 and 2544, and wasm lib.rs:4136-4137: "as few as pay".

No guard downstream: no UI string claims this (en.json has no "as few"). The review note names what is merged, never that fewer boxes would pay.

Why low
- Each sentence with "as few as pay" also states the Unknown rule that overrides it. So it contradicts itself in one edge case rather than making a flat promise. Only architecture.md's closing sentence is flatly too wide.
- Nobody has to act. It needs a box of unknown making that is larger than the known boxes, plus a merge the known boxes can't pay alone. Such a box comes from a planted box, Bring every box back now, the retired pools' run, or a box Koios hasn't answered for yet.
- The cost: one more box linked (B2 joins W, which whoever planted W can follow) and 45,608 lovelace more fee.
- In that case W is spent either way, so the extra box does nothing for the rule's own goal.
